reviewer: Codex source audit and selected actual-pixel inspection; agent review only
purpose: Find the corrected Unit 5 M15 generic-speaker ambiguity pattern in the other current missions.
implementation_scope: Separate older mission-content findings remain unchanged by this scoped Unit 5 patch. This record performs no implementation and grants no release or human semantic approval.
method: Read all non-voice-gate cue/answer text in all seven current missions, then inspect the actual full-resolution image pixels for the five findings and one contextual exception below.
limitations: The text scan covered all seven missions; image inspection was limited to the six selected suspect/contextual scenes listed here.
Lower-confidence findings retain contextual evidence and require deliberate follow-up review.
No broad tests or device interaction were run for this read-only audit.
Specific objects, food or actions are not flagged merely because their phrase includes a polite word.

findings.observed_pixels: Four disconnected people face mostly toward the viewer: a yellow-jacket girl raises her hand, a man holds a map, a red-coat woman points into the distance, and an older man shrugs with open palms.
findings.concern: No definite question-to-reply pairing. A hand can greet or interrupt, pointing does not uniquely mean Yes, and a shrug does not uniquely establish Sorry, no. The exact speaker assignments rely on interpreting generic poses.
findings.possible_follow_up: Review a specific initiating turn and response through the established two-view exchange, retaining required language and meaningful listening coverage.

findings.observed_pixels: At an information booth, a woman holds a map with one palm open, a man shrugs with two palms open, a girl cups an ear, and an older man raises a palm. All face the viewer.
findings.concern: The map holder and shrugging person could both need help or not understand. Cupping an ear and raising a hand do not reliably distinguish repeat from speak slowly. These exact phrases lack uniquely defensible targets.
findings.possible_follow_up: Review a specific initiating turn and response through the established two-view exchange, retaining required language and meaningful listening coverage.

findings.observed_pixels: A boy offers a ball to a smiling man with palms together. A girl holds an open book toward another girl who raises a palm.
findings.concern: Ball and book offers provide stronger context than the other flagged crowds. The responses still depend on one-frame gesture interpretation; review their reply targets as contextual exchanges without discarding the visibly specific play/read cues.
findings.possible_follow_up: Review a specific initiating turn and response through the established two-view exchange, retaining required language and meaningful listening coverage.

findings.observed_pixels: In one morning courtyard with an 8:00 wall clock, a foreground woman waves and a uniformed man at a doorway also waves while turning toward it. A seated reader and boy playing with a ball provide distinct action targets.
findings.concern: Light and clock establish morning, but two waves do not reliably distinguish greeting from farewell. The single frame does not clearly establish arrival versus departure; preserve the clear reading and playing cues.
findings.possible_follow_up: Review a specific initiating turn and response through the established two-view exchange, retaining required language and meaningful listening coverage.

findings.observed_pixels: A registration-table woman gestures toward a man with his hand on his chest; an entering woman waves; two older women talk on a bench.
findings.concern: Registration, familiar cast and arrival provide context, so this is lower confidence. Hello still relies on selecting a waving arrival from a static social scene; review whether preceding story evidence identifies her uniquely. This does not label every other cue on the card defective.
findings.possible_follow_up: Review a specific initiating turn and response through the established two-view exchange, retaining required language and meaningful listening coverage.

resolved_in_current_unit5_patch.previous_problem: One four-target cafe crowd assigned Can I have water, please?, Yes, please., No, thank you., and Tea, please. to people without a definite exchange.
resolved_in_current_unit5_patch.resolution: The established two-view mission voice gate shows a concrete bag offer, then the same customer accepting; the learner speaks the reply instead of guessing a speaker in a crowd.
resolved_in_current_unit5_patch.evidence_basis: Canonical bindings rechecked here; picture inspection and immutable provenance are recorded by the implementing bag-sequence media agent. This audit does not grant human approval.

contextual_exception_reviewed.observation: The targets are objects: a 5:00 clock, a price board, clear water carafes and three red apples. Water has a visible object target rather than an arbitrary person.
contextual_exception_reviewed.disposition: Outside this generic-speaker ambiguity finding; no change proposed by this audit.

coverage_constraint.requirement: Future changes must preserve invitation, acceptance/refusal and communication-help functions on successful paths and restore meaningful listening coverage as needed. Do not lower the floor or remove required language.

negative_scan_result: No remaining non-voice-gate crowd cues using Me too., Me neither., Yes, please., or No, thank you. were found in Units 1, 2, 4 or 5. This text-query result is not visual clearance of those missions.
